title: the Kama Sutra's ethics chapter (not the rest)
hook: before a word on love, the book recites its family tree
carry: the Kama Sutra's ethics chapter (not the rest)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Kama Sutra's ethics chapter gave each aim of life its season, with an honest note that life is uncertain. Today, before any of that, the book stops to say where it came from.

The wedding hasn't started and an uncle already has the microphone. Before anyone dances, he walks the room through the family: whose son, whose grandson, which village, which great-grandmother opened the sweet shop. A few people roll their eyes. Then they lean in, because the list says who belongs to whom. An old book famous for something else entirely opens the same way. Before a single word on love, the Kama Sutra stops and recites its family tree. And the name at the very top is a surprise.
screen: `AN UNCLE WITH THE MICROPHONE.` → `WHO BELONGS TO WHOM.` → `A BOOK THAT OPENS WITH ITS FAMILY TREE.`

segments.voice: At the top is Prajapati, the creator. In the book's opening, he sets down one vast teaching on how people should live. Not three books. One. Then the teaching is divided among three heirs. Manu takes the part on dharma, doing right. Brihaspati takes the part on artha, wealth and a living. And Nandi, Shiva's attendant, takes the part on kama, pleasure and love. Later teachers keep shortening and splitting their shares, the text says, until the pieces are scattered. Vatsyayana, the author, says he gathered them back into one small book. So notice what the family tree does. A book on desire doesn't introduce itself as a rebel or a secret. It introduces itself as a sibling of the law books, with the same parent. In this telling, kama was never outside dharma. All three aims begin as one plan for one life, and split only because the plan grew too big for anyone to carry. That's why this path reads the ethics chapter and leaves the rest on the shelf. The rest is a frank handbook for adults. The opening is an argument about how three aims fit together in one person, and its first move is to say: we're family.
screen: `ONE TEACHING FROM THE CREATOR.` · `DIVIDED AMONG THREE HEIRS.` · `GATHERED AGAIN BY VATSYAYANA.` · `A SIBLING OF THE LAW BOOKS.` · then, large: `THREE AIMS, ONE PARENT.`

segments.voice: Take a scrap of paper and write three short lines: one thing you do because it's right, one thing you do for a living or for school, and one thing you simply enjoy. Above them, draw a single line joining all three, like a family tree with one parent. Then sit with the page, ranking none of them.
The Kama Sutra's ethics chapter: the book's opening, where pleasure, right living and wealth come down from one teaching.
screen: `THE KAMA SUTRA'S ETHICS CHAPTER — today's word`.

segments.voice: Keep this one: the Kama Sutra's ethics chapter, not the rest, where all three aims share a parent. Day fifteen ninety-seven, done.

screen: `DAY 1597 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: A BOOK ON PLEASURE, AGAINST PLEASURE?`

fork.setup: your family's restaurant was split among three cousins long ago: one runs the kitchen, one the books, one the catering. you're writing its story for the menu. how would the Kama Sutra's opening tell it?

fork.reveal: the book starts at the top, with Prajapati's one teaching, then shows it divided among Manu, Brihaspati and Nandi. the split is part of the family story, not a scandal.

chat.meaning: The Kama Sutra's opening traces dharma, artha and kama to one teaching: pleasure is one part of a whole life, not its boss or its enemy.
